To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the order-fulfilment process of a capital good supplier is affected by the updating process of demand distribution as time passes, the supplier's risk aversion, and the cost structure.

(1) the supplier should start production earlier when the uncertainty of the lead time is higher, and when the supplier is less risk averse, (2) the supplier should also start production earlier when holding costs and the cost of cancellation are higher, and (3) the supplier should wait longer when the cost of delay is higher.

(1) the supplier's risk aversion plays a major role on the optimal time of production; (2) the supplier's optimal order-fulfilling strategy depends on the updating rule of the demand arrival-time distribution, and the supplier may choose a strategy that is different from the one suggested in the literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the supplier's order-fulfilling process in a customized industry.
a fundamental issue in supply chain management: how the supplier decides to fulfill the customer's order.
the supplier's order fulfillment process, which has been largely ignored by the existing literature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supplier's risk aversion and how the distribution is updated are two important factors that explain the supplier's conservatism in the order-fulfilment process.
both cost factors and the supplier's attitude toward risk are important in explaining the order-fulfilment process of the supplier.
the supplier is conservative because he is risk averse, and he is risk avert because he faces high cancellation and holding costs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the supplier should not be too conservative in starting the order fulfillment, especially in industries where the lead time is short.
, when a supplier has high risk aversion and a long lead time, it would start producing much earlier than what the cost model would suggest.
the supplier's risk aversion and demand updating play a significant role in determining when the supplier should start production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supplier's risk aversion is a major factor that determines the order-fulfilment time.
a model that captures the risk attitude of the supplier is needed to understand the supplier's behavior in the order fulfillment process and to design better policies for the supply chain.
risk attitude and demand distribution updating are important factors in the order-fulfilment process and should be considered when designing the supply chain.
